title: The purge that wasn't

loopNote: The reel ends in mayaTight: Maya at the same desk, in the same lamp light, giving the camera a flat, deadpan look. The first frame is the same mayaTight framing with her hands flying to her cheeks in panic. On a replay the cut plays as her next panic starting straight after she swore she would check first.
caption:
Maya's best post vanished from Google, and she was sure the big AI cleanup had taken it. Then she actually checked.

Before you blame Google, open Search Console, paste the page's link into URL Inspection and read the reason it gives. If it says "URL is not on Google" with "URL marked noindex", a setting on your own site is hiding the page. It's often a "show in search results" switch on the post. Turn it back on. Other reasons, like "Crawled, currently not indexed", need a different fix, so read the line before you change anything. You can also click Request indexing, but that only asks Google to look again. It doesn't promise anything.

Who's the friend who blames Google before checking anything? Send them this. (Maya and Floey are from Flowra.)
topic: Maya's best post vanished from Google, and she's sure the AI-content cleanup took it. Search Console names the real reason: she noindexed it herself.
editorNotes: Hook: "They're purging AI pages. They took mine!" sounds like Maya admitting her best post is an AI page. That makes her the slop blogger, not the viewer on a bad day. The joke only works if she believes the purge hit her human post by mistake. Change the line so it says so (for example, add "...and I wrote mine myself!"), keeping the problem in the first two seconds.

Tip: "Paste the link into URL Inspection" is a tool name with no plain version, and Search Console is never mentioned anywhere in the reel. A blogger who has never opened it can't do this today. Name Search Console in Floey's line, or at least put "Search Console" in the insert title (for example "Search Console: URL Inspection"), so the viewer knows where to go.

The timing can't work. After Floey's tip line, a 0.6 s pause has to hold the cut to wide, Maya pasting and pressing enter, the whoosh, four rows ticking in one by one and the ring growing on the rise. That is about 3 s of action and five or more sounds, and the rule is at most one sound every 0.4 s. Either set this gap to about 2.5 to 3 s (pushing Maya's read), or start the typing during Floey's line. The same problem hits the 0.4 s gap after "Oh.": the Post settings insert, the Off to On click and the ding can't fit before "So it just...". Give the fix its own silent gap of about 1.5 s.

"Every time, Maya." is untrue. URL Inspection doesn't always give a usable reason. 'Crawled - currently not indexed' gives no why, and the brief says it is usually a quality matter. If the page is indexed but has lost ranking, it just says 'URL is on Google'. The brief also notes that indexing isn't guaranteed. Floey is always right, so she can't overclaim. Use a line that is true, such as one about it telling you where to look first, or cut this exchange (see the polish note).

The button doesn't follow. Maya says "Google, I'm so sorry" and Floey answers "Google says you're welcome", but "you're welcome" answers a thank you, not an apology. Viewers will hear it as a mistake, not a punchline, so the ending fizzles. Either Maya thanks Google (and Floey takes the credit for Google), or Floey gives an answer that fits a sorry (for example, Google forgives her and Floey doesn't). Keep it to the two running jokes.

(polish) "So it just... tells you why?" / "Every time, Maya." is the writer's moral in the characters' mouths, and it sags between the realisation ("Oh.") and the button. Maya already read the reason two lines earlier, so the question rings false. Think about cutting both lines and going from the silent fix straight to the button. That also shortens the reel.

(polish) Faces and voices don't match. In the check beat the voice is 'worried' but the face on "Who did that?" is annoyed, so pick one (the indignant read fits better, with 'determined' as the voice). In the button the voice is 'warm' but the face is sheepish and sad. Also, the doubt line is voiced 'determined' over an annoyed face, while the cast says Maya goes flat when annoyed. Make each face match its line's feeling.

(polish) Some sound and behaviour names aren't in the kit. 'keyboard tap' should be typing {d}, 'enter-key clack' should be click, and 'preen rustle' should be Floey's own preen or swish. 'Puffs her chest' isn't a listed Floey behaviour, so use pivot front plus a tilt or a preen. Floey 'turns toward the laptop' while she is perched on it, so describe a look down at the screen instead. A chip sfx on top of her spoken 'It does' will muddy the line, so put it just before.
(polish) Post settings insert: the ring grows on a 'click' sfx, but nobody clicks there. Use tick or rise, and keep click for Maya's real Off to On fix so each sound stays one real event.

(polish) Hook frame: on frame one the '0 clicks' pill and the '!' should already be up, not popping in, because the problem is already happening. In mayaTight the stat spot (about x 880, y 610) and the '!' above her bun may land off frame or above y 220. Place both by hand inside the safe area and check the still at phone size.

(polish) Insert row 'Last crawl' / '1 day ago (example)': the sub-line already marks this as an example, so the extra '(example)' clutters the value. Measure it so it fits the value column. The brief had '3 days ago'; either works with 'last Tuesday', but keep one.

(polish) The loop note says the replay reads as her next panic 'straight after she swore she would check first', but she never swears that in the script. Duo reels don't need a loop note anyway. Fix it or drop it.

(polish) The reframe beat says Maya is 'frozen' in the cheeks pose. The listener is never frozen, so add a small move on Floey's 'why' (a blink, a slow lowering of her hands) as well as the eye slide.
(polish) "Best post, gone from Google!" is clipped and sounds written. "My best post is gone from Google!" (as in the brief) is how a panicking person talks and costs almost nothing in time.
